name: BQE Central (the triple cantilever)
address: I-278 from Atlantic Ave to Sands St, under the Promenade
eyebrow: NYC DOT · CEQR 26DOT006K · Brooklyn Community District 2
intro: The city-owned 1.5-mile stretch of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway from Atlantic Avenue to Sands Street, with 21 bridges and structures, including the 0.4-mile triple cantilever built in 1954 that carries the Brooklyn Heights Promenade [[scope]]. The city plans to rehabilitate it, not replace it, using temporary bypass highways while the cantilever is repaired [[mayor26,scope]].

status.headline: Scoping is underway; written comments are still open
paragraphs: Mayor Mamdani announced the plan on Aug 24, 2026: a full rehabilitation of the existing structure, said to extend its life about 40 years, to around 2080 [[mayor26]]. NYC DOT issued the Draft Scope of Work for the environmental impact statement on Oct 2, 2026 [[scope]] and held public scoping meetings on Nov 10 (in person, City Tech) and Nov 12 (Zoom) [[enb1007,dotpage]].

The written comment deadline was Nov 23, 2026 in the official notice [[enb1007]]; press reports it was extended to Jan 11, 2027 [[sb1116]]. DOT's page hadn't been updated when last checked, so confirm with DOT before relying on the later date. Comments go to BQECentral@dot.nyc.gov [[dotpage]].

Next: a Final Scope in early 2027, the Draft EIS with a public hearing in late 2027, and the Final EIS in 2028 [[dotpage]]. The sources disagree on when construction starts: 2029 in the Draft Scope [[scope]], 2030 in the Mayor's announcement [[mayor26]]. Work would finish before 2040 [[scope]]. Some parkland changes would need a ULURP starting around 2028 [[sb1116,faq]].

facts: Rehabilitate all 21 structures; replace the Columbia Heights overpass superstructure; new drainage and railings [[scope]]
Two each way, as today; no new capacity or interchange changes [[scope]]
A temporary two-level highway over Furman St, Atlantic Ave to Columbia Heights, below the Promenade [[scope]]
From Columbia Heights, possibly above the Brooklyn Bridge approach, through Dumbo to west of the Manhattan Bridge [[scope,sb1001]]
More than 130,000 vehicles a day, about 13,000 of them trucks [[scope]]
No federal grants; ~$800M in applications were rejected in 2024 [[politicsny]]

track.intro: The city is the lead agency for a state and city environmental review (CEQR/SEQR), not the federal NEPA process [[scope]]. Dates after today are DOT's targets [[dotpage]].

steps.t: DOT proposes a temporary highway on the Promenade; withdrawn after opposition

watch.p: The Promenade sits on the structure. DOT says it will keep portions open "to the extent feasible" [[faq]]; press reports say parts will close [[sb0824]].

The two-level bypass would run over Furman St, as close as four feet to 360 Furman (about 1,200 residents), per a building representative [[sb1116]]. DOT says park access stays open and it doesn't plan impacts to Brooklyn Bridge Park; the EIS will study shadows [[faq,scope]].
Squibb Park, Hillside Dog Park, Anchorage Plaza, Clumber Corner, Bar and Grill Park and Adam Yauch Park are affected; Harry Chapin Playground would be rebuilt [[scope,sb1001]].

The EIS will model air quality and noise (14 measurement sites) and study three state-designated Disadvantaged Communities near the work, plus cumulative effects with the Brooklyn Marine Terminal redevelopment [[scope]].

The Brooklyn Heights Association calls the scope "far too narrowly defined" with "only one option", while welcoming no added lanes [[brownstoner,sb1116]]. Council Member Restler, State Senator Gounardes and Assembly Member Simon called the temporary highways "invasive and disruptive" [[sb1116]].
The Columbia Heights rezoning next door expects DOT's BQE work near the site to start in 2029, its own build year [[chpd]]. See the Columbia Heights tab.
